matchstick.title: Vertical sticks in simple numerals
matchstick.principle: I, II, III, and L are composed only of vertical matchsticks, so adding or removing a single vertical stick changes the numeral’s value by one.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral consists solely of vertical sticks and you need to adjust its value by ±1.
matchstick.example: Changing I (1) to II (2) by adding a vertical stick increases the value by one.

matchstick.title: Preserve token validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, both the source character (with a stick removed) and the destination character (with a stick added) must still be valid Roman numerals or allowed operators (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick; always verify that both tokens remain legal.
matchstick.example: You cannot remove the only vertical from I because it would disappear, leaving an invalid token.

matchstick.title: Use numeric difference to guide moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of each side of the equation; the difference indicates how many units the total must increase or decrease, helping you decide which stick to move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is false; use the gap to target a ±1 or ±2 adjustment.
matchstick.example: If left side is 9 and right side is 16, you need to add 7 to the left or subtract 7 from the right.

matchstick.title: I‑V reordering changes value by 2
matchstick.principle: Moving an I across a V (changing IV to VI or vice‑versa) flips the I from subtractive to additive position, altering the numeral’s value by two.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains IV or VI and you need a ±2 adjustment.
matchstick.example: IV (4) → VI (6) adds 2 to the value.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from one numeral to another reduces the source’s value by one and raises the destination’s value by one, shifting the overall balance accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust two numerals in opposite directions by one.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical from II (2) to III (3) yields I (1) and IV (4).

matchstick.title: Never take sticks from V or X
matchstick.principle: V and X are built only from diagonal sticks; removing any diagonal destroys the character, so they cannot be sources for stick moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a potential source is V or X; avoid taking sticks from them.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from X would leave a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity
matchstick.principle: When moving sticks involving operators, the resulting symbol must still be one of the allowed operators (+, -, =). For example, removing the vertical from '+' yields '-', and adding a vertical to '-' creates '+'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick is moved from or to an operator.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' to a numeral turns '+' into '-' and adds an I to the numeral.

matchstick.title: Final verification of equation
matchstick.principle: After performing a stick move, recompute the values of all numerals and check that the arithmetic holds; also ensure every token is a valid numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you think you have a solution; always double‑check the arithmetic and token validity.
matchstick.example: After moving a stick, verify that 9 = 13 - 4 is true.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick from '+' to numeral
matchstick.principle: Moving the vertical component of a '+' operator to a numeral simultaneously changes '+' to '-' and adds an I to the numeral, increasing its value by one.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to both change a '+' to '-' and increase a numeral by one.
matchstick.example: Changing 'XII + IV' to 'XIII - IV' by moving the vertical from '+' to the 'XII'.

matchstick.title: Horizontal stick transfer between operators
matchstick.principle: A horizontal stick can be moved from the '=' sign to a '-' sign (or the reverse), turning '-' into '=', and '=' into '-', while keeping both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to replace a subtraction with an equality (or vice versa) without altering numerals, and a horizontal stick is available from another operator.
matchstick.example: Turning 'A = B - C' into 'A - B = C' by moving a horizontal from '=' to '-'.

matchstick.description: Taking a stick from V or X, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: V and X consist only of diagonal sticks; removing one leaves a single diagonal, which does not correspond to any valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never use a diagonal stick from V or X as a source; only take vertical sticks from numerals that contain them.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid one
matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick can unintentionally alter an operator into a shape that is not +, -, or =.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move involving an operator, verify that the resulting symbol is still one of the allowed operators.

matchstick.description: Assuming a single stick can change a numeral's value arbitrarily
matchstick.why_it_happens: Not all numerals can be altered by a single stick; some require specific configurations.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Know which numerals are built from vertical sticks (I, II, III, L) and which are not; only those can be changed by one vertical stick.

matchstick.description: Neglecting to recompute the arithmetic after the move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver may focus on the stick manipulation and forget to check the resulting numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the values of both sides after a move and confirm the equation holds.

matchstick.description: Treating diagonal sticks as interchangeable with vertical sticks
matchstick.why_it_happens: Diagonal and vertical sticks have different orientations; swapping them changes the shape and often invalidates characters.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation; only move vertical sticks to positions that require vertical orientation, and diagonal sticks to diagonal positions.
